title: Fynaptix · Space Economy Research
heading: Space Economy Intelligence
subheading: Launch, satellites, constellations & the post-SpaceX-IPO landscape
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. Space is capital-intensive with heavy government-customer concentration. Verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.label: SpaceX's first earnings after the June IPO beat ($12.7B consensus) as AI ('Super Intelligence') hit $7.56B, now ~52% of revenue, and Starlink connectivity grew 69% to $5.25B; but Q3 capex was $19.6B and Q4 is guided to $35–40B, mostly AI, so it is increasingly not a pure space story. Starship Flight 15 (first attempted ship catch) is listed NET Nov 8 by Wikipedia but only 'November, TBD' by launch trackers.

kpis.sub: SPCX OCT 30 CLOSE · -6.4% ON THE DAY · ~40% BELOW $225.64 JUNE HIGH
kpis.label: The post-earnings pop faded: SPCX closed $134.72 on Oct 30 in a sector-wide small-cap selloff, below the ~$148 level after the Oct 20 print. Merger committees at SpaceX and Tesla are still studying a combination (no terms; Barclays calls it a key part of the Tesla bull case); the next big supply event is ~797.6M shares around Dec 8 (third-party schedule, verify against the prospectus).

kpis.sub: RKLB OCT 30 CLOSE · -7.4% ON THE DAY · -23% IN OCTOBER · Q3 REPORT NOV 9
kpis.label: Q3 guidance is revenue $250–265M (vs $155M a year ago), adjusted EBITDA loss $17–23M and non-GAAP gross margin 35–37% (41.5% in Q2); market cap ~$32.75B. Neutron's first flight is now 2027 with no new date, a ~$1.94B stock sale in September helps fund the $8B Iridium deal (IRDM holders approved Sept 24; close guided mid-2027).

kpis.sub: Q3 2026 PRIVATE SPACE INVESTMENT · RECORD QUARTER
kpis.label: Seraphim counts 216 deals in Q3 (median $9.8M) versus $7.4B in Q2; Blue Origin's ~$10B round is nearly half the total, so excluding it the quarter is still ~$10.8B. Blue Origin said Oct 16 that Florida infrastructure investment has passed $3B.

tiers.label: Scale Players
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list.

rows.angle: Q3 revenue $14.58B (+161%), net income $4.4B, adjusted EBITDA $8.8B; Starlink connectivity $5.25B (+69%) with ARPU about $69 and ~13.6M consumer subscribers (press reports); Starship flew its first revenue mission in September and Flight 15 is expected in November, attempting booster and ship catches.
rows.watch for: Q3 capex of $19.6B and a $35–40B Q4 guide (mostly AI), ~797.6M shares of lockup supply around Dec 8, unresolved Tesla merger talks (no terms, shareholder vote needed), Starship Flight 15 timing (NET Nov 8 per Wikipedia, 'November TBD' elsewhere) and Starshield political risk. Shares $134.72 on Oct 30.

rows.angle: Q2 revenue $234.1M (+62%), backlog $2.36B (+137%), Q3 revenue guided to $250–265M; the $8B Iridium deal (~$27 cash plus stock, ~$54 per IRDM share) is approved by Iridium holders and guided to close mid-2027; Iridium Q3 revenue $245.7M (+8%).
rows.watch for: Neutron slipped to 2027 (at least the third delay, no new date); shares closed $54.73 on Oct 30 (-23% in October); Q3 results Nov 9 after the close (adjusted EBITDA guided to a $17–23M loss, gross margin 35–37%), dilution from the ~$1.94B September stock sale, and FCC review of Iridium.

rows.angle: Q3 (Oct 29) revenue $6.1B (+7%, +9% organic), GAAP EPS $3.28 (+33%), record backlog $53.2B and 3.2x book-to-bill; FY26 EPS guide raised to $12.25–12.35 and revenue to $23.5–23.7B; Space & Mission Systems grew double digits, anchored by 18 of the 36 satellites in the SDA's $1.75B Tranche 3 tracking award.
rows.watch for: Space & Mission Systems book-to-bill was only 1.0x (the 3.2x total is driven by Missile Solutions at 11.8x), debt of $11.0B, and conversion of the Tranche 3 awards. Also sits in the Defense sleeve — don't double-count exposure. Share price not captured this run.

rows.watch for: Shares ~$10.4 on Oct 30 (-11% that day, -27% in October); Q2 operating cash burn of $59.8M, equity of about -$290M, $235M raised through an at-the-market offering (dilution), and ~$259M of net insider selling over 12 months.

rows.angle: Q2 revenue $116.05M (+58%, beat), fifth straight EPS beat, adjusted EBITDA $13.9M; part of Google's Project Suncatcher prototype and won a NASA Tanager task order.
rows.watch for: Price not refreshed this run (~$13.4–13.9 in late October, ~63% below Apr 20); Barclays' $17 target (Equal Weight) implies limited upside; dependence on SpaceX rideshare capacity and founder stock sales.

rows.watch for: GAAP loss of $0.54 per share (miss) including a $10.5M derivatives loss; shares ~54% below Apr 20; full-year revenue against $130–150M guidance.

private_watchlist.name: Blue Origin
private_watchlist.note: Reported ~$10B raise at a ~$130B valuation (its first outside round, described as oversubscribed). On Oct 16 it announced a $330M Rocket Park phase at Cape Canaveral with two more New Glenn pads, saying Florida investment has passed $3B; New Glenn returns to flight after the May pad explosion at LC-36 — year-end 2026 per some reports, early 2027 per Blue Origin's own update — with multi-vehicle operations targeted for summer 2027.

private_watchlist.name: Firefly Aerospace
private_watchlist.note: Already public, so it is outside the private groups; no fresh company news found this week. Not given a stance here for lack of current data.

private_watchlist.name: Stoke Space
private_watchlist.note: No new update this week beyond the earlier $1B Series E (total raised $2.3B); Nova Block 2, a fully reusable design, remains targeted for 2029.

bear_case.title: Capital intensity
bear_case.description: SpaceX spent $19.6B of capex in Q3 and guides $35–40B for Q4, mostly for AI; Rocket Lab (which sold ~$1.94B of stock in September) still guides to a $17–23M Q3 adjusted EBITDA loss while funding an $8B Iridium deal; Blue Origin needed a ~$10B raise. Funding is abundant now, but the sector depends on it staying that way.

bear_case.title: Government concentration
bear_case.description: The SDA's Tranche 3 tracking awards ($1.75B across L3Harris and Sierra Space in July) and Redwire's NITE STAR slot (one of 15 vendors, no guaranteed revenue) show how much revenue hangs on a few federal programs. Starshield restrictions in Ukraine show a single operator's decisions can become a geopolitical issue.

bear_case.title: SpaceX dominance and supply overhang
bear_case.description: SPCX closed $134.72 on Oct 30, ~40% below its June high, with ~797.6M lockup shares due around Dec 8 and a possible Tesla merger adding uncertainty; its spectrum purchase and Starlink Mobile put it directly against AST SpaceMobile, and AI is now over half its revenue, so owning it is no longer a clean space exposure.

bear_case.title: Binary mission risk and schedule slips
bear_case.description: Neutron's first launch slipped into 2027 (at least the third delay, no new date), AST had a BB7 launch incident and has 13 satellites against a ~45 target, New Glenn is grounded until year-end or early 2027, and Starship's catch and refuelling remain unproven (Flight 15 timing unconfirmed). RKLB fell 23%, ASTS 33% and LUNR 27% in October alone.

catalysts.title: SpaceX Q3: revenue $14.6B (+161%), net income $4.4B
catalysts.description: Beat on revenue and EPS; AI segment $7.56B, Starlink connectivity $5.25B, Q4 capex guided to $35–40B. Musk said SpaceX and Tesla formed special committees to study a merger (no terms agreed).

catalysts.title: Iridium beats Q3 estimates
catalysts.description: EPS $0.98 vs $0.34 expected, revenue $245.7M (+8%); the Rocket Lab takeover (~$54 per share) is guided to close mid-2027.

catalysts.title: Small-cap space selloff reverses
catalysts.description: LUNR +9% and RKLB +7% in a rebound after earlier weakness, with SpaceX lagging.

catalysts.title: L3Harris Q3 beats and raises
catalysts.description: Revenue $6.1B (+7%), GAAP EPS $3.28, record $53.2B backlog; FY26 EPS guide raised to $12.25–12.35. Space & Mission Systems grew double digits but book-to-bill was 1.0x.

catalysts.title: Space stocks sell off again
catalysts.description: RKLB -7.4% to $54.73, LUNR -11% to ~$10.4, SPCX -6.4% to $134.72; for October RKLB is -23%, ASTS -33% and LUNR -27%.

catalysts.description: Commentary only; SpaceX and Tesla committees are still studying a combination, with no terms and a shareholder vote required.

etfs.name: Procure Space
etfs.summary: Pure-play, revenue-weighted (RKLB, PL, ASTS among top holdings); has tracked the weakness in the mid-cap names through the October selloff. No fresh price captured this run.

etfs.name: ARK Space Exploration
etfs.summary: Actively managed with broader tech adjacency; ARK has commented that Neutron comes close to Falcon 9 on payload, and the fund's results depend heavily on a handful of high-beta holdings. No fresh fund data found this week.

etfs.name: SPDR Kensho Final Frontiers
etfs.summary: Equal-weight blend of space, defense and deep-sea names; the defense-adjacent holdings (like L3Harris) cushion it versus pure-plays, though L3Harris itself has lagged since July. No fresh fund data found this week.

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: Rocket Lab
positions.note: Neutron's slip into 2027 and a 23% October drop to $54.73 hurt sentiment, and Q3 gross margin is guided down to 35–37%, but Q2 revenue of $234.1M (+62%), a $2.36B backlog and Q3 guidance of $250–265M (reported Nov 9) keep the Electron-led business intact.

positions.name: L3Harris
positions.note: Q3 beat with a record $53.2B backlog, GAAP EPS $3.28 and FY26 EPS guidance raised to $12.25–12.35, though Space & Mission Systems book-to-bill was only 1.0x. Also sits in the Defense sleeve — don't double-count exposure.

positions.name: Planet Labs
positions.note: Q2 revenue of $116.05M (+58%), a fifth straight EPS beat and $13.9M adjusted EBITDA are the best fundamentals among the small caps, but ~$13.4 is still 63% below April and Barclays' $17 target shows limited upside.

positions.name: Intuitive Machines
positions.note: Q2 revenue of $206.2M and a $1.76B backlog are real, yet equity is about -$290M, a $235M at-the-market raise is diluting holders and the stock fell 27% in October to ~$10.4, so it stays small.

positions.name: AST SpaceMobile
positions.note: A Q2 revenue miss ($31.5M vs $34.4M), a $125.9M BB7-related loss, Piper Sandler's downgrade and SpaceX's spectrum push outweigh $1.3B of backlog; the stock fell 33% in October to ~$39, but falling is not yet cheap.

positions.name: Redwire
positions.note: A $542M record backlog and a Q2 beat ($117.1M revenue) are encouraging, but adjusted EBITDA is still −$3.2M, NITE STAR carries no guaranteed revenue and insiders have been heavy sellers at ~$8.4.

positions.name: BlackSky
positions.note: Q2 revenue of $33.3M (+50%) with positive adjusted EBITDA of $4.7M is good progress, but a GAAP loss of $0.54 per share and a ~54% drop since April leave the earnings quality unresolved.

positions.name: SpaceX
positions.note: Q3 revenue of $14.6B (+161%) and $4.4B net income are strong, but AI is now over half of revenue, Q4 capex is guided to $35–40B, ~797.6M lockup shares are due around Dec 8 and the stock slid to $134.72, with Tesla merger terms still unknown. UK investors wanting indirect exposure can use Scottish Mortgage (SMT, covered on the Baillie Gifford page).

positions.name: Iridium Communications
positions.note: Q3 EPS of $0.98 vs $0.34 expected was a clean beat, but the deal (~$27 cash plus Rocket Lab stock, ~$54 per share, closing mid-2027) ties it to RKLB's slide — RKLB remains the cleaner way to express the view.
